title: Finite type field points and finite residue extensions
statement: Let $V$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $l$ a field [def-weil-field], and $f:\operatorname{Spec}l\to V$ a morphism [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $v$ be its image point and put $k=\kappa(v)$ [def-weil-residue-field], with the induced field embedding $k\to l$. The following are equivalent: (i) $f$ is of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; (ii) $f$ is locally of finite type; (iii) there is an affine open neighbourhood $W=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $v$ such that $v$ is closed in $W$ and $[l:k]<\infty$. In this case the canonical morphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to V$ is of finite type.

source.place: Tag 01TA (lemma-point-finite-type), equivalence (1), (2), (4); last assertion follows by the closed-point factorization in the affine open.

proof.text: The spectrum of $l$ has one point. The inverse image under $f$ of any affine open of $V$ is therefore either empty or this singleton, hence quasi-compact. By the definition of finite type, (i) and (ii) are equivalent. This argument applies to every morphism from the spectrum of a field, including the canonical morphism from $\operatorname{Spec}k$.

Assume (ii). Choose an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ containing $v$. The all-affine-pairs criterion says that the corresponding map $A\to l$ makes $l$ a finitely generated $A$-algebra. Its kernel is the prime $\mathfrak p$ of $v$, and $k=\kappa(v)$ is the fraction field of $R=A/\mathfrak p$, embedded in $l$. The same algebra generators show that $l$ is finitely generated over the image subring $R\subset l$. Apply the subring-localization lemma to obtain $0\ne s\in R$ with $R_s$ a field and $l/R_s$ finite.

source.place: Tag 01TA (lemma-point-finite-type), (2) implies (3), through the application of Algebra Tag 00FY

proof.text: Lift $s$ to $a\in A$. Then $a\notin\mathfrak p$ and $W=D(a)$ is an affine neighbourhood of $v$ with coordinate ring $A_a$. Localization commutes with quotient, giving $A_a/\mathfrak p A_a\cong(A/\mathfrak p)_s=R_s$. Since this is a field, $\mathfrak p A_a$ is maximal, so its singleton is closed in $\operatorname{Spec}A_a$: a prime containing this maximal ideal equals it. Moreover the fraction field of $R$ equals $R_s$: each nonzero element of $R$ has its inverse in the field $R_s$, and every element of $R_s$ is a fraction in $R$. Thus the induced embedding identifies $k$ with $R_s$, and $[l:k]<\infty$. This proves (iii).

source.place: Tag 01TA (lemma-point-finite-type), end of (2) implies (3) and closed-point interpretation (3) implies (4)

proof.text: Assume (iii), and write $W=\operatorname{Spec}A$ with prime $\mathfrak p$ for $v$. Closedness means $\mathfrak p$ is maximal: its closure is the primes containing $\mathfrak p$, and a maximal ideal containing it would otherwise give a second point in that closure. Hence $A/\mathfrak p$ is a field. The affine residue-field description identifies $k=\operatorname{Frac}(A/\mathfrak p)=A/\mathfrak p$, with the specified embedding into $l$. Take a finite $k$-basis of $l$. Since $A\to k$ is surjective, every linear combination of the basis has coefficients lifted from $A$; these basis elements therefore also generate $l$ as an $A$-algebra. The pointwise affine-pair criterion, applied to the sole point of $\operatorname{Spec}l$ and the target open $W$, gives (ii).

Under these equivalent conditions retain the same $W$ and the identification $k=A/\mathfrak p$. The canonical morphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to V$ is induced on $W$ by the quotient $A\twoheadrightarrow k$. A quotient is generated as an algebra by the empty family, so the pointwise affine-pair criterion makes this canonical morphism locally of finite type. The singleton argument of step 1 makes it quasi-compact, hence of finite type.
